question: Which customers mentioned integrations with Salesforce?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every statement about integrations with Salesforce (or Salesforce-related CRM connectors), including what was requested, promised, built, available, or limited, and the speaker's role (customer or OrbitFlow staff). Note the company's call type and whether the mention came from an existing customer or a prospect.
assumptions: 'Customers' is read broadly to include any company on the call that mentioned Salesforce integration, since the question does not restrict call type.
Synonyms for Salesforce include SFDC and general CRM integration terms, since transcripts may abbreviate the name.

findings.speaker: Rachel Morgan
findings.quote: That's the core, yeah.
findings.context: Rachel Morgan (prospect, Acme Logistics) agreed that Salesforce is part of the core stack, which she listed as the systems involved in their process. — Prospect discovery/first demo call (CALL-001). Weak, indirect mention: she confirmed Maya's playback of the stack, which included Salesforce, rather than naming Salesforce herself.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: opportunity closes in Salesforce, create the onboarding plan, assign tasks based on product mix
findings.context: OrbitFlow's proposed phase-one pilot workflow is triggered by an opportunity closing in Salesforce, then creates an onboarding plan and assigns tasks. — Prospect discovery/first demo call (CALL-001). Vendor proposal for a single representative workflow, not a built or confirmed integration.

findings.speaker: Rachel Morgan
findings.quote: That's the right shape.
findings.context: Rachel Morgan (prospect) accepted the Salesforce-triggered onboarding workflow as the right shape for phase one, with the caveat that the happy path is not the hard part. — Prospect discovery/first demo call (CALL-001). Acceptance of the vendor proposal, with a caveat about edge cases and failure handling.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: you'd said Salesforce is mandatory
findings.context: Maya Chen restated that Acme's customer-side team said Salesforce is mandatory for the integrations. — Prospect discovery/first demo call (CALL-001). This is the vendor summarising the customer's earlier position, not the customer's own words.

findings.speaker: Rachel Morgan
findings.quote: The system of record. If that connector's unreliable, none of the rest matters.
findings.context: Rachel Morgan (prospect) said the Salesforce system-of-record connector is the deal-breaker: if it is unreliable, nothing else matters. — Prospect discovery/first demo call (CALL-001). Answering the question about the Salesforce integration; she does not name Salesforce explicitly in this turn.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: For your stack it's a mix of native connectors and API-based options.
findings.context: OrbitFlow said its connectivity to Acme's stack, which includes Salesforce, is a mix of native connectors and API-based options, and that a pilot should validate each required operation rather than rely on the integrations page. — Prospect discovery/first demo call (CALL-001). Vendor claim that does not name Salesforce explicitly; it is an implication from the stack discussion. No Salesforce connector is confirmed as built or available.

findings.speaker: Martin Vogel
findings.quote: SAP S/4HANA. Salesforce. ServiceNow. Microsoft Teams.
findings.context: DeltaWorks lists Salesforce as part of its current systems stack, alongside SAP S/4HANA, ServiceNow, Microsoft Teams and on-premise SQL Server systems. — CALL-004, DeltaWorks Manufacturing, prospect, enterprise discovery call. Customer describes its current stack. No Salesforce connector, API or integration method is discussed for this system.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: A large service contract closes in Salesforce.
findings.context: OrbitFlow proposed a phase-one workflow in which a large service contract closes in Salesforce, then customer and product data is validated against SAP, ServiceNow tasks are created, and mismatches are escalated before order processing. — OrbitFlow staff (AE Maya Chen) describing a candidate use case. This is a proposed design, not a confirmed or built integration. The customer said the description was close but said the valuable part was the early mismatch escalation.

findings.speaker: Martin Vogel
findings.quote: That is close. The last part is the valuable part.
findings.context: The customer said the Salesforce-based phase-one candidate was close to right, with the early mismatch escalation at contract close being the most valuable part. The customer did not say how Salesforce would be connected. — Customer response to the OrbitFlow proposal in T090. Customer correction at T093 concerns where mismatches are currently caught, not Salesforce connectivity.

findings.speaker: Noah Williams
findings.quote: Salesforce, Snowflake, Slack, Okta, Jira, and an internal event bus. Required: all of those, plus webhooks and a generic REST connector.
findings.context: Customer lists Salesforce as a required integration for the phase-one stack, alongside Snowflake, Slack, Okta, Jira, and an internal event bus. — Prospect call (CALL-005, Ember Financial, Evaluation, 2026-07-02). Noah Williams is VP Operations Technology and the executive sponsor. This is a stated requirement, not a confirmed capability; OrbitFlow later says connectors are to be validated in a pilot rather than by logo.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: Enrich them from Salesforce and Snowflake.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff (Nina Patel, Solutions Engineer) plays back the phase-one candidate use case as enriching partner onboarding events from Salesforce and Snowflake. — Prospect call (CALL-005). This is OrbitFlow's restatement of the customer's use case, not a confirmed product claim about a Salesforce connector. The customer confirms the playback ('That's it.') at T071.

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: the proposal, as I understand it, is to combine Zendesk ticket patterns, Salesforce account status, and Snowflake product usage to flag accounts needing proactive intervention
findings.context: Darren Wu proposed combining Zendesk ticket patterns, Salesforce account status, and Snowflake product usage to flag accounts needing proactive intervention. This is the requested Salesforce integration in a prospect evaluation call (Inkwell Learning, not an existing customer). — Customer (prospect) restating the proposed cross-system use case; requested integration, not yet built

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: If Salesforce fields are stale, an elegant workflow will still make bad decisions.
findings.context: Darren Wu is concerned that stale Salesforce fields would make a Salesforce-dependent workflow produce bad decisions. — Data-quality concern about Salesforce as an input to the proposed integration

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: Salesforce is reliable for the commercial facts — contract dates, ARR, owner. It is unreliable for anything a human has to remember to type.
findings.context: Darren Wu says Salesforce is reliable for commercial facts (contract dates, ARR, owner) but unreliable for fields humans must type. — Customer's assessment of Salesforce data trustworthiness, relevant to which Salesforce fields could feed the integration

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: queries the warehouse, joins against the CRM, and evaluates a set of conditions.
findings.context: OrbitFlow's Jon Bell describes the example workflow as joining warehouse data against the CRM, which would include Salesforce, though Salesforce is not named explicitly. — Vendor demo description of the pattern; the CRM is not named as Salesforce, so the link to Salesforce is an inference

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Human-maintained fields are context you show to the person, not inputs the logic depends on.
findings.context: Maya Chen proposed that Salesforce human-maintained fields be shown as context to the user rather than used as inputs the logic depends on. — Vendor design recommendation for how Salesforce data is used in the proposed flag logic; not explicitly named as Salesforce

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: nothing joins Zendesk to Snowflake to Salesforce in a way that produces an action.
findings.context: Darren Wu says nothing currently joins Zendesk, Snowflake, and Salesforce in a way that produces an action, and that Salesforce fields are overwritten with no history. — Customer describing current state; the Salesforce gap is a limitation of existing tooling and of data history

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: Salesforce, no. Salesforce fields get overwritten, there's no history on most of them.
findings.context: Jon Bell notes that the Salesforce human-maintained fields should not carry the flag, which Darren Wu agrees with because Salesforce has no point-in-time history for backtesting. — Vendor and customer agree Salesforce human fields are excluded from the flag; the data limitation (no history) aligns with the design decision

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.quote: Salesforce API limits are the constraint. We've hit them before.
findings.context: Salesforce API limits are a constraint for the customer's integration design, and they have hit those limits before. — Customer (prospect Staff Software Engineer) raising Salesforce API limits as a known constraint, in response to OrbitFlow's rate-limit answer.

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.quote: I'd have to check. It's not generous.
findings.context: The customer's Salesforce daily API allocation is not generous, and she needs to check the exact number. — Customer declining to give the exact figure on the spot; OrbitFlow asked for it.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: Get me the number and I'll tell you honestly whether the design fits inside it. If it doesn't, the answer might be batching or caching rather than more API calls.
findings.context: OrbitFlow asked the customer for their Salesforce daily API allocation and said it will assess whether the design fits within it; if not, batching or caching would be the fix. — OrbitFlow Solutions Engineer; conditional technical commitment pending the customer's number.

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.quote: Or not using Salesforce as a live lookup.
findings.context: The customer proposed avoiding Salesforce as a live lookup to stay within API limits, and OrbitFlow agreed to design around that. — Design mitigation proposed by customer for the Salesforce API constraint; OrbitFlow accepted it.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: That's scoped on the Salesforce side by the permissions of the user or integration account you connect with. We use what you give us. We don't have a separate layer that further restricts it.
findings.context: Salesforce permissions are controlled upstream by the user or integration account used to connect; OrbitFlow adds no separate permission layer on top. — OrbitFlow explaining least-privilege scoping for a Salesforce connection; the customer had asked whether objects could be scoped.

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.quote: If a workflow retries a step that writes to Salesforce, do I get two records?
findings.context: The customer asked whether a retried workflow step writing to Salesforce could create duplicate records. — Customer technical concern about idempotency of Salesforce writes; it was a test of whether OrbitFlow would overclaim.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: If the downstream system isn't idempotent and the write succeeded but the response was lost, then yes, potentially.
findings.context: OrbitFlow said a retry could create duplicate Salesforce records if the downstream API is not idempotent and the write succeeded but the response was lost; OrbitFlow cannot make a non-idempotent API idempotent, though retries are visible in the run record. — OrbitFlow answer to the Salesforce duplicate-record question; no overclaim.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: Just confirm what I've got. Salesforce, Segment, PostgreSQL, Slack, Linear, internal services, AWS.
findings.context: OrbitFlow's Solutions Engineer listed Salesforce as part of the customer's stack to confirm. — Stack confirmation during technical evaluation; Salesforce is one of several named systems.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: the Salesforce API allocation
findings.context: OrbitFlow asked the customer for their Salesforce API allocation as an action item for the evaluation, and the customer agreed to provide it. — Follow-up action list at call close; the customer agreed to provide it.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: combine product and CRM signals
findings.context: The intended use case includes combining product and CRM signals to drive operational tasks, which implies a CRM integration (Salesforce is not named in this turn). — OrbitFlow's summary of the use case; CRM is generic here, and Salesforce is named elsewhere in the call.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: it was a retry storm caused by a Salesforce outage on their side
findings.context: OrbitFlow's Maya Chen attributed the March retry storm (about 20,000 runs) to a Salesforce outage on Salesforce's side. This is an outage, not a described Salesforce integration. No customer named Salesforce in this call, and Devan Shah only referred to the March retry storm. — Vendor speaker (OrbitFlow AE) on a renewal/QBR call with existing customer Lumen Retail Group. Mention is of a Salesforce outage affecting run volume, not a stated integration, build, or limitation. Customers Fiona Bright and Devan Shah did not mention Salesforce.

This is requested, not built.

Salesforce permissions are scoped on the Salesforce side by the connecting account. Nina's stack confirmation listed Salesforce.

DeltaWorks Manufacturing (prospect): Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications) listed Salesforce in its stack with SAP S/4HANA, ServiceNow, Microsoft Teams and on-premise SQL Server. Maya Chen proposed a workflow starting when a large service contract closes in Salesforce. Martin said it was close and that early mismatch escalation was the valuable part. No Salesforce connection method was discussed.

Lumen Retail Group (renewal): Maya Chen attributed the March retry storm (about 20,000 runs) to a Salesforce outage on Salesforce's side. This is an outage, not a described integration, and Lumen's Fiona Bright and Devan Shah did not mention Salesforce.
